question: A legal operations manager writes project instructions containing forty numbered rules intended to cover every request the team might ever make. What is the most likely consequence?
options: A) Each numbered rule creates a separate chat history, so the project's conversations are split across rules.
B) Numbered lists are not accepted in the instructions field, so only the first several rules are stored at all.
C) Long instructions force the project into retrieval mode, which removes uploaded documents from answers.
D) Rules that rarely apply crowd out the few that always matter, so the key ones are followed less reliably.
correct_answers: D) Rules that rarely apply crowd out the few that always matter, so the key ones are followed less reliably.
explanations: Instructions do not create or partition chat histories in any way.
There is no restriction on numbered lists in project instructions.
Retrieval behaviour relates to the size of project knowledge, and it does not remove documents from answers.
Correct. Long, undifferentiated rule lists dilute the direction that actually matters for most requests.
